(The provided excerpt cuts off before the exact constraint formulation; the full PDF is needed to specify the precise algorithm and hyperparameters.)
- Chat-vector interpretation: the log-probability difference can be viewed as a text-space projection of the parameter delta θ_post − θ_pre, making the distilled signal usable for any student model regardless of architecture.
- Pipeline: generate (instruction, response) pairs with CoDIT, then SFT students on the resulting dataset; compare against standard teacher decoding and against existing public instruction datasets.
summary_en.experiments:
Across nine teacher–student pairs, students trained on CoDIT-generated responses outperform those trained on standard teacher-generated responses on WildBench and AlpacaEval 2.0. The released CoDIT datasets also surpass several existing instruction-tuning datasets cited in the paper.
(The excerpt you provided does not include the experiment section/tables, so I cannot report exact model sizes, dataset sizes, or numeric gains without guessing. With the complete PDF, I can extract the full result tables, ablations on post-training stages, and sensitivity to contrastive-decoding hyperparameters.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Deep-read plan (1.5–2 hours with the full PDF):
1) Method details: precisely how the constrained contrastive decoding is implemented (candidate filtering, thresholds, any re-ranking), since this governs output quality.
2) Theory section: how the paper formally connects log p_post − log p_pre to the chat vector and what assumptions are required for cross-architecture transfer.
3) Main results: check consistency across all teacher–student pairs; pay attention to whether smaller students benefit more (supporting the “pretrained knowledge as noise” claim).
4) Ablations: expert model variants (SFT-only vs RLHF-added), contrast strength, and any quality metrics (format adherence, verbosity, factuality).
5) Qualitative examples: verify what “knowledge suppression” looks like in practice (less encyclopedic content vs better instruction compliance).

recommendation.zh: 改变我对“合成SFT数据越多越好”的prior：应抑制teacher的知识成分、蒸馏post-pre增量；建议立刻在自家teacher上复现。
recommendation.en: Updates the “more synthetic SFT is better” prior: explicitly suppress teacher pretrain-knowledge and distill the post-pre delta; I’d replicate this on our teachers ASAP.

paper.title: Self-Distillation Zero: Self-Revision Turns Binary Rewards into Dense Supervision
paper.abstract: Current post-training methods in verifiable settings fall into two categories. Reinforcement learning (RLVR) relies on binary rewards, which are broadly applicable and powerful, but provide only sparse supervision during training. Distillation provides dense token-level supervision, typically obtained from an external teacher or using high-quality demonstrations. Collecting such supervision can be costly or unavailable. We propose Self-Distillation Zero (SD-Zero), a method that is substantially

summary.core_problem: 解决强化学习（RLVR）在可验证任务中二元奖励信号过于稀疏、样本效率低的问题，且无需依赖外部强模型提供密集监督。
summary.importance: 方法创新，提出了一种在无需外部Teacher的情况下，将稀疏二元奖励转化为密集Token级监督的自蒸馏范式，对提升推理模型（如O1-like RL）的训练效率极具启发。
summary.technical_approach: 提出Self-Distillation Zero (SD-Zero)，让单一模型扮演Generator和Reviser两角。Reviser基于Generator的初始回复和二元奖励生成改进回复，随后通过同策略自蒸馏将Reviser的Token分布作为软标签蒸馏给Generator。
summary.experiments: 在无需外部Teacher和高质量演示的情况下，SD-Zero的训练样本效率显著高于传统依赖稀疏奖励的RL方法。
summary.authors_note: 普林斯顿大学 Danqi Chen 与 Sanjeev Arora 团队出品，理论与实证结合的顶尖组合。

summary_en.core_problem: Addressing the sparse supervision and low sample efficiency of Reinforcement Learning (RLVR) with binary rewards in verifiable settings, without relying on external strong models.
summary_en.importance: Methodological innovation proposing a self-distillation paradigm that converts sparse binary rewards into dense token-level supervision without an external teacher, highly relevant for training reasoning models (e.g., O1-like RL).
summary_en.technical_approach: Introduces Self-Distillation Zero (SD-Zero), where a single model acts as both Generator and Reviser. The Reviser generates an improved response conditioned on the initial response and its binary reward. On-policy self-distillation is then used to distill the Reviser's token distributions into the Generator.
summary_en.experiments: Demonstrates substantially higher training sample efficiency compared to standard RL methods relying on sparse rewards, without needing external teachers or high-quality demonstrations.
summary_en.authors_note: From Princeton University, led by Danqi Chen and Sanjeev Arora, representing top-tier research combining theory and empirical methods.

recommendation.zh: 巧妙利用Reviser将稀疏二元奖励转化为密集的Token级监督，直击当前RLVR样本效率低的痛点，建议立刻在内部推理模型的后训练pipeline中验证其有效性。
recommendation.en: Elegantly converts sparse binary rewards into dense token-level supervision via a self-playing Reviser; highly relevant to current RLVR pipelines and should be ablated internally.

paper.title: English is Not All You Need: Systematically Exploring the Role of Multilinguality in LLM Post-Training

summary.core_problem: 在“后训练（SFT）阶段”语言覆盖高度英语中心化的现实下，系统性回答：在控制数据规模不变（使用平行翻译数据）时，增加后训练语言覆盖度会如何影响（1）英语与非英语的性能权衡，（2）不同任务形态（数学推理 vs 结构化API调用），以及（3）不同模型规模/家族下的干扰与迁移；并检验“多语种诅咒/负干扰”在后训练阶段是否同样显著。
summary.importance: 对基座研究的直接启发在于：多语种带来的“容量稀释/负干扰”在后训练阶段并不必然出现，至少在作者控制变量的设定下，语言覆盖度提升总体呈现“低资源持续受益、高资源平台化而非退化”，且“加入一个非英语语言”往往就能带来跨语言泛化（甚至对英语也有增益）。这会影响你如何设计SFT数据配比（language coverage 作为一等公民的scaling维度）、如何评估跨语种能力是否来自预训练还是后训练，以及如何用平行数据做更干净的因果对照。另一个贡献是提出并公开可复现生成脚本的多语种API调用数据集 mAPICall-Bank，为研究多语种tool-use提供了更标准的起点。
summary.technical_approach:
核心方法是“受控多语种覆盖度scaling实验设计”，而非提出新训练算法。
1) 变量控制：用平行翻译的任务数据构造多语种混合物，随着语言数从1扩到最多10，保持每种语言采样相同数量样本，从而让‘语言覆盖度’变化尽量不与‘总样本量增加/数据多样性增加（非平行）’混淆。
2) 任务与数据：
- 数学推理：训练用 mCoT-MATH（11语种、CoT解答），每语种采样1万训练、200验证；测试用 MGSM（每语种250题），用对应语言的“Let’s think step by step”触发CoT。
- API调用：构建 mAPICall-Bank（基于 API-Bank 的API calling子任务），用SOTA LLM翻译成11语种；每语种3174训练、399测试，训练/测试API不重叠，另留150验证；评测通过解析输出提取API invocation。
3) 模型与规模：两条模型家族（Qwen-3：0.6B/1.7B/8B；Gemma-3：1B/4B），共220次SFT runs，形成“语言覆盖×模型规模×任务域”的网格。
4) 关注点：不仅看‘包含某语言’的直接收益，也看‘未包含语言’的零样本迁移随覆盖度变化的曲线，从而区分“直接监督”与“多语种多样性带来的泛化”。
summary.experiments:
全文给出的关键结论是趋势型而非单点SOTA：
- 多语种覆盖度提升整体“利大于弊”：低资源语言随覆盖度增加持续提升；高资源语言更常见的是性能平台化而非下降，英语也并非必然受损。
- ‘最小多语种’有效：在英语任务SFT中加入哪怕单一非英语的平行数据，通常就能带来跨语言（含英语）收益，说明英语-only后训练在该设定下系统性次优。
- 高覆盖度带来更强零样本迁移：当语言多样性足够高时，对未显式加入的语言也能出现接近“直接加入该语言”的效果；但对类型学距离更远、且低资源的语言仍存在局限。
- 设计层面的关键：由于使用平行数据，收益更可信地归因于“语言覆盖/多样性”而非“数据量变大”。
（注：你提供的全文片段在API评测解析与结果表格处截断，未包含可逐条引用的具体数值表；若需要精确到每个setting的提升幅度/方差/显著性，需要补齐结果章节与附录表格。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约30–45分钟）：
1) 先看 Figure 1（语言覆盖度scaling设定）与 Table 1（评测语言选择与资源属性），理解“覆盖度”如何被操作化。
2) 重点读 Experimental Details：尤其是“平行采样1万/语种”“MGSM评测方式”“mAPICall-Bank构建与API不重叠划分”，这是论文因果可信度的关键。
3) 结果部分建议按两条主线读：
- 覆盖度从1→N时，英语/高资源是否退化（验证是否真的没有‘curse’）。
- 未包含语言的zero-shot曲线是否随N上升（验证‘多样性带来迁移’而非仅仅‘监督覆盖’）。
4) 若你做数据科学/配比：重点关注作者如何固定总量、如何采样、以及不同任务（推理 vs 结构化生成）是否呈现一致趋势。

summary_en.core_problem: Post-training (SFT) for LLMs is still overwhelmingly English-centric. This paper asks, under a controlled setup where dataset size is not confounded with language coverage (via parallel translations), how scaling the number of languages in post-training affects (i) English vs. non-English trade-offs, (ii) different capability domains (math reasoning vs. structured API calling), and (iii) different model families/scales—i.e., whether the “curse of multilinguality/negative interference” meaningfully manifests in post-training.
summary_en.importance: For foundation-model researchers, the main takeaway is that multilinguality in post-training can be a net positive across tasks and scales in a controlled regime: low-resource languages keep improving as coverage grows, while high-resource languages (including English) tend to plateau rather than degrade. Even adding a single non-English language often improves cross-lingual generalization beyond the added language, suggesting English-only SFT is systematically suboptimal. Methodologically, the paper is valuable as a clean causal-style study design (parallel data mixtures) and as a new multilingual tool-use dataset (mAPICall-Bank) that can seed more rigorous multilingual tool-use research.
summary_en.technical_approach:
This is primarily an experimental/scaling study rather than a new optimizer or architecture.
1) Controlled multilingual scaling: construct post-training mixtures by adding more languages (up to 10) while sampling the same number of parallel examples per language, aiming to isolate “language coverage/diversity” from “more data”.
2) Tasks/datasets:
- Math reasoning: train on mCoT-MATH (11 languages, CoT solutions), 10k train + 200 val per language; evaluate on MGSM (250 problems per language) with language-specific CoT trigger prompts.
- API calling: introduce mAPICall-Bank by translating API-Bank’s API-calling subtask into 11 languages using a strong LLM; 3,174 train + 399 test per language, with disjoint APIs across splits; evaluation parses API invocations.
3) Models/scales: Qwen-3 (0.6B/1.7B/8B) and Gemma-3 (1B/4B), totaling 220 SFT runs to map interactions among language coverage, scale, and domain.
4) Analysis focus: measure both in-language gains and zero-shot transfer to languages not included in training mixtures, to separate “direct supervision coverage” from “diversity-driven generalization.”
summary_en.experiments:
Reported findings are largely trend-level:
- Increasing language coverage during post-training is broadly beneficial across tasks and model scales; low-resource languages benefit the most.
- High-resource languages, including English, typically plateau rather than regress as multilinguality increases.
- Minimal multilinguality helps: adding just one non-English language often yields gains that generalize to other languages (sometimes including English).
- High-diversity mixtures enable strong zero-shot cross-lingual transfer that can approach the effect of explicitly including the target language in low-diversity settings, with remaining weaknesses for typologically distant low-resource languages.
Note: the provided full-text excerpt is truncated before the main results tables/figures; exact per-setting numbers (deltas, variance, significance) require the complete results/appendix sections.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (30–45 minutes):
1) Start with the experimental design figure (language-coverage scaling) and the table describing evaluated languages (resource level/script/family).
2) Read the Experimental Details carefully—parallel sampling, fixed per-language counts, MGSM evaluation protocol, and mAPICall-Bank construction/split rules are the credibility backbone.
3) In results, track two curves: (a) English/high-resource performance vs. coverage (does interference appear?), and (b) zero-shot performance on held-out languages vs. coverage (does diversity drive transfer?).
4) If you care about data mixing/scaling, focus on how they operationalize “coverage” under a fixed-budget constraint and whether the two task types behave similarly.

recommendation.zh: 只看实验矩阵与配比结论：用平行数据控变量后，多语SFT未必“容量稀释”，可把language coverage当一等scaling维度来配数据。
recommendation.en: Focus on the controlled parallel-data ablations: it weakens the “multilingual SFT dilutes capacity” prior and suggests treating language coverage as a first-class scaling knob in SFT mixing.

paper.title: Correct Prediction, Wrong Steps? Consensus Reasoning Knowledge Graph for Robust Chain-of-Thought Synthesis

summary.core_problem: 论文聚焦“答案正确但推理步骤不可靠”的结构性失配：LLM 可能通过带有逻辑错误/幻觉的中间步骤（Step Internal Flaws），或通过过度/不足推理（Step-wise Flaws：overthinking/underthinking）仍得到正确最终答案。作者进一步提出并验证一个反直觉问题：即便给定正确最终答案，让模型“只需解释”，也并不能稳定提升推理步骤质量或整体推理能力；因此需要一种能在样本级同时处理多类混合缺陷的统一后处理/合成框架。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接价值不在于提出新的预训练目标，而在于为“用 CoT 作为训练/蒸馏数据”的数据科学提供了强约束：1）仅用正确答案条件化并不能净化推理轨迹，说明轨迹缺陷主要来自中间结构与局部决策而非答案不确定性；2）提出“跨轨迹共识”作为自动化筛噪与补全的原则，可用于构建更高保真推理数据（SFT/RL/蒸馏）并降低把错误推理写入基座模型的风险；3）从方法论上把 over/underthinking 与 step-level 逻辑错误统一到同一检测与合成管线，提示后续在 RL pretrain/持续学习中应把‘轨迹结构一致性’作为可优化信号，而不是只优化 outcome reward。
summary.technical_approach:
CRAFT（Consensus Reasoning knowledge graph Aggregation for Flaw-aware Traces synthesis）是一个“多轨迹→共识结构→拓扑生成”的统一框架，核心思想是：同一题目采样得到的多条推理轨迹中，大多数步骤在语义与结构上是可对齐且正确的；错误/冗余/缺失步骤会在跨轨迹比较中表现为偏离共识。

模块 I：多样化轨迹生成与共识术语抽取。对每个样本 rollout K 条候选推理轨迹；用 TF-IRF（文中表述为 TF-IRF weighting）从多轨迹中抽取“共识术语/关键概念”T_con，用于后续对齐与图构建时的锚点，降低纯文本表述差异带来的噪声。

模块 II：共识 RKG 构建与异常过滤。将每条轨迹转为 Reasoning Knowledge Graph（RKG）：节点=推理步骤，边=逻辑关系（有向）。再把多条 RKG 聚合为共识图 G*：直观上保留多数轨迹共享的节点/边结构。随后用统计过滤（文中提到 z-score filtering）剔除结构上显著偏离的步骤/子结构，以同时捕捉两类缺陷：
- Step Internal Flaws：内容错误/幻觉导致该步骤与其他轨迹难以形成一致的语义-结构邻接；
- Step-wise Flaws：overthinking 表现为少数轨迹额外插入的冗余分支；underthinking 表现为少数轨迹缺失共识中的关键节点/边。
该“组内相对比较”的思想与 GRPO 的 group relative comparison 类似：不依赖外部标注逐步判错，而用组内一致性作为弱监督信号。

模块 III：拓扑引导的轨迹合成。对共识图 G* 做拓扑序遍历（topological order），按图结构生成一条高质量推理轨迹：既避免冗余（不走被过滤的偏离分支），又补齐关键步骤（沿共识主干覆盖必要节点），从而在不显式使用正确答案条件化的情况下提升最终预测与轨迹质量。
summary.experiments:
论文在两类互补评测上验证“给答案不提升推理”的结论与 CRAFT 的收益：
1）PRMBench：把 LLM 当 verifier 来识别错误步骤，衡量逐步可靠性；
2）ROSCOE：衡量生成推理轨迹的多维质量。
在 w/ Answer 与 w/o Answer 两种设置、跨 4 个 LLM 的系统评估中，给定正确最终答案总体“无一致提升”，部分情形还会下降，支持作者关于“问题在中间步骤结构与缺陷混合”的诊断。

在方法对比上，CRAFT 在逻辑与数学推理基准上平均带来 10%+ 的 label-prediction accuracy 提升，并在多种基线下保持一致优势；同时在细粒度轨迹质量评测维度上也更好。由于你提供的全文片段未包含完整实验表格与具体模型/数据规模/每个基准的逐项数值，无法在此可靠复述参数量、K 的取值、各数据集上的精确提升幅度与显著性检验细节。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 20–35 分钟）：
- 先读 Section 4.1（或对应实验小节）：作者如何设计“w/ Answer vs w/o Answer”的对照、在 PRMBench/ROSCOE 上如何度量“推理能力/轨迹质量”，以及哪些情况下给答案会变差。
- 再读 Methodology/Algorithm 1：重点看三模块接口（TF-IRF 共识术语→单轨迹 RKG→聚合成 G*→z-score 过滤→拓扑生成），理解它如何同时覆盖 internal flaw 与 step-wise flaw。
- 关注 RKG 的定义：节点/边如何从自然语言步骤抽取、聚合时如何对齐（共识术语在其中的作用），以及过滤阈值对 over/underthinking 的敏感性。
- 若你关心预训练数据科学：重点思考 CRAFT 生成的“高质量轨迹”能否作为蒸馏/持续学习数据，哪些环节可能引入偏置（例如共识会不会压制少数但正确的解法）。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a persistent mismatch in LLM reasoning: models can output the correct final label while producing unreliable chain-of-thought steps. It argues that failures are heterogeneous and sample-specific—mixing step-internal errors (logical mistakes, hallucinations) with step-wise issues (overthinking/underthinking). A key empirical question is tested: even when the correct final answer is provided and the model is asked to justify it, reasoning quality and robustness do not improve consistently, implying the root cause lies in intermediate-step structure rather than answer uncertainty.
summary_en.importance: Its main value for foundation-model researchers is as a data/trajectory quality result rather than a new pretraining objective. It provides evidence that “answer-conditioned justification” is not a reliable way to clean CoT traces, which matters for distillation and RL-style training where traces become supervision. The proposed cross-trace consensus principle suggests a scalable way to filter, repair, and synthesize higher-fidelity reasoning trajectories—potentially reducing the risk of imprinting flawed reasoning into base models. Conceptually, it reframes over/underthinking and step-level logical errors as a unified, consensus-detectable phenomenon, hinting that future RL pretraining could incorporate structural-consistency signals beyond outcome rewards.
summary_en.technical_approach:
CRAFT (Consensus Reasoning knowledge graph Aggregation for Flaw-aware Traces synthesis) is a multi-sample post-processing framework that turns multiple candidate traces into a single higher-quality trace via a consensus reasoning graph.

Module I: Generate K diverse candidate traces per problem and extract consensus terms using TF-IRF weighting. These terms act as anchors to reduce surface-form variance across traces.

Module II: Build a per-trace Reasoning Knowledge Graph (RKG) where nodes are reasoning steps and directed edges encode logical relations. Aggregate per-trace graphs into a consensus graph G* and filter anomalous steps/structures using z-score-based deviation filtering. The same mechanism is intended to catch (a) step-internal flaws, which tend to diverge semantically/structurally from the majority, and (b) step-wise flaws, where redundant branches (overthinking) or missing backbone steps (underthinking) are exposed by comparing each trace to the group consensus. The design is explicitly motivated by group-relative comparison ideas (akin to GRPO).

Module III: Synthesize a final trace by traversing the consensus graph in topological order, producing a coherent step sequence that follows the majority-supported backbone while avoiding filtered deviations.
summary_en.experiments:
The paper evaluates the “provide the correct answer” hypothesis and the CRAFT framework on two complementary benchmarks: PRMBench (LLM-as-verifier for erroneous-step identification) and ROSCOE (multi-dimensional reasoning-trace quality). Across four LLMs and two settings (with vs without the correct answer), providing the answer yields no consistent gains and sometimes degrades performance.

For end-task performance, CRAFT reports 10%+ average improvements in label-prediction accuracy across logical and mathematical reasoning benchmarks and also improves detailed trace-quality metrics. The provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete result tables (model sizes, dataset sizes, per-benchmark deltas, K values), so exact numeric breakdowns cannot be reproduced here without risking fabrication.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (20–35 minutes):
- Read the section reporting the w/Answer vs w/oAnswer study (notably the PRMBench/ROSCOE protocol and metrics) to understand why answer-conditioning fails.
- Then read the method/Algorithm 1 end-to-end: TF-IRF consensus term extraction → per-trace RKG construction → consensus aggregation and z-score filtering → topology-guided synthesis.
- Pay special attention to how RKG edges are defined/extracted from natural language steps and how graph alignment is done; these details determine whether consensus preserves correct minority solution paths.
- If your interest is pretraining data pipelines, focus on the discussion/implications for distillation and RL training: when consensus helps, when it might collapse diversity, and how to tune filtering thresholds.

recommendation.zh: 只看“正确答案条件化也洗不干净CoT”的证据与共识合成管线：它改变我对用CoT当训练数据的信心，应立刻加到内部轨迹筛噪里。
recommendation.en: Focus on the evidence that conditioning on the correct final answer doesn’t sanitize CoT, and the consensus synthesis pipeline—this should directly change how you filter/construct reasoning traces.

paper.title: SFT-GRPO Data Overlap as a Post-Training Hyperparameter for Autoformalization

summary.core_problem: 在“先 SFT、后 GRPO”的 Lean4 自动形式化后训练流水线中，SFT 阶段与 GRPO 阶段训练提示（prompts）数据的重叠比例是否会系统性影响最终性能？如果会，最佳实践应是让两阶段数据尽量不重叠还是复用同一批数据？
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对后训练/持续训练的数据科学有明确启发：1）把“SFT 与 RL 阶段数据重叠”提升为一个可控超参，并用严格对照实验显示其对效果有单调影响；2）提示一个常被忽视的机制：当 GRPO prompts 与 SFT 数据高度重合时，RL 阶段可能主要在强化已记忆/已拟合的轨迹，边际收益接近 0；而使用不重叠 prompts 更像是在做分布外的策略改进与泛化增强；3）提出并实证 compile pass@k 与 semantic pass@k 的巨大鸿沟（>30pp），对“只看可编译率”的评测范式提出警示；4）给出面向 RL 训练的 answer injection 数据处理，使得“只做形式化不做求解”的任务设定在 RL 中可行。这些结论可迁移到更一般的 SFT+RL 配方（不仅限 Lean）。
summary.technical_approach:
方法是严格控制变量的配方消融：
- 基座：Qwen3-8B（thinking disabled）。
- 任务设定：只生成 Lean4 theorem 声明，结尾用 := by sorry，使编译通过不依赖证明搜索，从而把学习信号聚焦在“陈述翻译”。
- 数据：四个公开来源（NuminaMath、Leanabell-Prover、HERALD、Lean Workbook），统一做编译验证、SHA-256 去重、质量过滤、主题分层、格式化等；SFT 集 20k 对；GRPO prompts 约 16k。
- 关键自变量：GRPO prompts 与 SFT 训练集的重叠比例（0%/30%/100%）。三种设置保持来源分布一致，仅改变交集大小，以隔离 overlap 的因果影响。
- GRPO 奖励：使用编译器反馈（并且 GRPO 端的 ground-truth Lean4 仅供 reward 计算，模型生成时不可见）。
- Answer injection：针对“find/determine”类题目，RL 阶段若不注入答案，模型必须先解题才能形式化，导致 GRPO-only 极差；作者从 ground-truth Lean4 用 12 类模式抽取具体答案并附加到 prompt，使 RL 学到的是形式化而非求解。
- 评测：Gaokao-Formal 与 PutnamBench；同时报告 compile pass@k 与由 LLM judge（阈值≥0.7）评估的 semantic pass@k，用于衡量语义忠实度。
summary.experiments:
六种条件：base、SFT-only、GRPO-only、以及 SFT+GRPO（overlap=0/30/100）。主要发现：
- overlap 越低，compile 与 semantic 指标单调更好；0% overlap 最优，100% overlap 基本“无增益”。
- 在 Gaokao-Formal 上，0% overlap 的 GRPO 相对 SFT-only 带来 10.4 个百分点的 semantic 提升（论文给出的明确数字）。
- compile 与 semantic 存在显著脱钩：对编译率最高的模型，compile-semantic gap 可超过 30pp，说明仅用 compile pass@k 会高估真实语义正确率。
- 观察性结论：GRPO-only 若不做 answer injection 会持续失败；answer injection 使得 GRPO 能在标准 SFT 数据上运作。
其余具体 pass@k 数值、不同 k 的曲线/表格需要从正文结果表中精读提取（你提供的片段未包含完整表格）。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 40–60 分钟）：
- Sec.1/实验设定：把握“overlap 作为唯一变量”的对照设计是否严谨。
- Sec.3 数据与清洗：重点看 dedup、编译验证、以及 answer injection（12 种模式）——这是让 RL 可训练的关键工程点。
- 结果部分：优先看 overlap=0/30/100 三组在 Gaokao-Formal、PutnamBench 的 compile vs semantic 对照表，理解单调性与 gap。
- 讨论：思考该结论对通用 SFT+RL（如指令跟随、代码、数学）是否成立：当 RL prompts 与 SFT 高重合时，是否等价于“对已拟合样本做 on-policy 再强化”，从而收益受限。
值得深挖：1）overlap 影响是否来自难度分布差异（作者声称来源分布一致但未形式化验证）；2）semantic judge 的可靠性与阈值敏感性；3）在更大模型/开启 thinking 的情况下单调性是否保持。

summary_en.core_problem: In an SFT→GRPO post-training pipeline for Lean 4 autoformalization, does the prompt overlap between the SFT corpus and the GRPO prompt set materially affect downstream quality, and if so, what overlap level is optimal under a controlled setup?
summary_en.importance: Not a pretraining-method paper, but highly relevant to post-training data science: it elevates SFT–RL data overlap into an explicit hyperparameter and shows (under tight controls) that lower overlap yields better results at no extra compute. It also highlights a major evaluation pitfall—compile pass@k can overstate true semantic faithfulness by >30pp—pushing the community toward dual-metric evaluation. The answer-injection pipeline is a practical contribution enabling RL on datasets originally designed for SFT, and the overlap finding plausibly generalizes to broader SFT+RL recipes where RL on memorized prompts provides little marginal policy improvement.
summary_en.technical_approach:
A controlled ablation with overlap as the only intended variable:
- Base model: Qwen3-8B (thinking disabled).
- Task framing: generate Lean 4 theorem statements ending with `:= by sorry` to isolate statement formalization from proof search.
- Data: four public corpora with compilation checks, SHA-256 dedup, filtering, stratification, and formatting; SFT uses 20k NL–Lean pairs; GRPO uses ~16k prompts.
- Overlap conditions: 0%, 30%, 100% of GRPO prompts coincide with the SFT set, while keeping source mixture constant.
- GRPO reward uses compiler feedback and hidden ground-truth Lean statements (used only for reward computation).
- Answer injection: extract numeric/concrete answers from ground-truth Lean via 12 pattern types and append them to “find/determine” prompts so RL trains translation rather than requiring the model to solve the math.
- Evaluation: Gaokao-Formal and PutnamBench with both compile pass@k and LLM-judge semantic pass@k (threshold ≥ 0.7).
summary_en.experiments:
Six training recipes: base, SFT-only, GRPO-only, and SFT+GRPO with overlap {0, 30, 100}.
Main results reported:
- Performance improves monotonically as overlap decreases; 0% overlap is best, 100% overlap yields near-zero gains from GRPO.
- On Gaokao-Formal, 0% overlap delivers a +10.4pp semantic improvement over SFT-only (explicitly stated).
- Compile vs semantic mismatch is large: compile–semantic gaps can exceed 30pp for the highest-compiling models.
- GRPO-only without answer injection performs poorly on “find the value” style problems; injection is necessary for RL viability in this setup.
Additional exact pass@k numbers by dataset/k should be taken from the paper’s result tables (not present in the provided excerpt).
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim (40–60 minutes):
- Intro + experimental design to verify overlap is isolated cleanly.
- Data section for dedup/compilation filtering and especially the answer-injection procedure (critical for RL feasibility).
- Results tables contrasting overlap=0/30/100 on both datasets, and the compile vs semantic gap analysis.
- Discussion: map the overlap effect to a general hypothesis—RL on overlapping prompts mostly reinforces already-fitted trajectories, limiting generalization gains.
Follow-ups to scrutinize: potential hidden difficulty shifts across overlap pools, robustness of the LLM-judge semantic metric, and whether the monotonic trend holds for larger models or with “thinking” enabled.

recommendation.zh: 把“SFT-RL prompts 重叠率”当超参做干净对照，这个结论可直接改你流水线；另只需看 compile vs semantic pass@k 的落差图，别再被可编译率骗。
recommendation.en: Treating SFT–RL prompt overlap as a tunable knob is immediately actionable for your pipeline; also just check the compile vs semantic pass@k gap figure—stop trusting compile-only metrics.

paper.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe

summary.core_problem: 论文聚焦 OPD（On-Policy Distillation，学生自采样轨迹、教师提供逐 token log-prob 作为稠密监督）在大模型后训练中“有时极其有效、有时完全失效”的核心不确定性：为什么更强的 teacher 反而可能无法提升 student？OPD 成功/失败由哪些可观测条件决定？其 token 级训练动力学与梯度信号到底来自哪里？以及如何把这些机制总结成可复现的训练配方来修复失败配置。
summary.importance:
对预训练/持续学习/训练动态研究的影响主要体现在“机制与配方”层面：
1) 给出 OPD 成功的两个必要条件（思维模式一致性 + teacher 必须带来 student 未见的新能力），把以往“teacher 更强→更好蒸馏”的直觉拆解为可检验的分布条件，为后续做 scaling/数据配比/持续蒸馏提供了诊断指标。
2) 提供 token 级机制证据：OPD 的有效梯度主要集中在 student-teacher 的 top-k 重叠 token 集合上；并展示成功运行的统一动力学签名（overlap 上升、entropy gap 收敛、概率质量集中）。这对理解“稠密监督为何有效/为何会失效”很关键，也能指导更稳健的蒸馏目标设计（例如只监督重叠集、或显式提升初始重叠）。
3) 给出可操作的修复 recipe（off-policy cold start、teacher-aligned prompt selection）并分析稠密监督随轨迹深度退化的成本，直接服务工业后训练流水线。

从基座研究视角，它不是新的预训练目标，但它把 OPD 作为一种“持续学习/自举式改进”的核心算子进行机制化解释，对未来 RL-pretrain、长链路推理蒸馏、以及 agentic 轨迹学习的稳定性研究都有直接启发。
summary.technical_approach:
全文结构是“现象学→机制→配方→成本/局限”的闭环。

(1) 现象学：两条成功条件
- 条件 A：Thinking-pattern consistency（思维模式一致）。作者用 student 与 teacher 的 top-k token 分布重叠度（overlap ratio）来刻画：如果初始重叠很低，即便 teacher benchmark 更高，OPD 也可能无法把 student 拉到 teacher 分布附近。
- 条件 B：Higher scores ≠ 新知识。即使思维模式一致、teacher 分数更高，如果 teacher 与 student 来自同数据同训练配方、只是 scale 更大，那么从 student 视角看 teacher 分布可能“不可区分”（distributionally indistinguishable），teacher 并没有提供 student 未见过的可迁移信号，OPD 增益会很小。
- 通过 weak-to-strong 的 reverse distillation 进一步验证：OPD 学到的本质是“思维模式/分布形状”，而不是简单地追逐 benchmark 分数。

(2) token 级机制：梯度信号的主承载体是 overlap tokens
- 成功 OPD 的统一签名：在 student 访问到的状态上，student 与 teacher 分布逐步变得更相似：top-k overlap ratio 持续上升；两者 entropy gap 逐渐缩小；重叠 token 集合承载了 97–99% 的联合概率质量。
- 失败 OPD：overlap 停滞、entropy mismatch 从一开始就存在并持续。
- 关键验证：只对“重叠 token 集合”施加监督，效果可匹配完整 top-k 监督，说明 OPD 的有效梯度主要来自重叠集；非重叠部分对优化贡献小或噪声大。

(3) Recipe：两种互补的失败修复策略
- Off-policy cold start：先用 teacher 生成的 rollouts 做一段 SFT warmup，提高初始 overlap，缩小思维模式差距，再切换到 OPD。
- Teacher-aligned prompt selection：用 teacher 后训练数据分布中的 prompts 来做 OPD，使监督集中在 teacher 高概率 token 上，更易对齐；但会导致 student entropy 显著降低（更“尖”/更保守），因此需要与 out-of-distribution prompts 混合以避免过拟合/塌缩。

(4) 稠密监督的成本与长轨迹问题
- reward 质量随 trajectory depth 系统性下降；不稳定性往往从后段 token 开始并向前传播。
- 重要观察：即便“失败 teacher”，其 reward 与 rollout 正确性在全局上仍相关，失败更像是局部优化几何问题：更大的 teacher 可能让 student 附近的 reward landscape 局部变平，导致 token 级梯度虽“方向正确”但幅度/曲率不足以推动策略更新。

整体上，作者把 OPD 从经验技巧提升为可诊断、可修复、可解释的训练算子，并给出一套与 token 分布几何直接对应的指标体系（overlap、entropy gap、probability mass concentration）。
summary.experiments:
从你提供的全文片段（引言+部分机制结论）中可以确定的关键数字/结论包括：
- 成功 OPD 的 top-k overlap ratio：从 72% 上升到 91%。
- 重叠 top-k token 承载的联合概率质量：97–99%。
- 只监督 overlap tokens 的实验：性能可匹配完整 top-k 监督（定性结论，片段未给具体分数）。
- 失败运行的特征：overlap 与 entropy gap 基本不动。
- reverse distillation 结论：同家族 1.5B 与 7B teacher 在 student 视角“分布不可区分”，因此即便 teacher 更强也可能不给增益。
- 长轨迹分析：reward 质量随深度下降，后段 token 先不稳定并向前传播；失败并非 reward 全局无信息，而是局部几何导致梯度无效。

但当前片段缺失大量你可能关心的“可复现细节数字”：具体 benchmark（数学/代码/指令遵循？）、OPD 目标形式（KL/advantage 形式/温度/截断 top-k 的 k 值）、训练步数与学习率、prompt 数量与来源、cold start 的长度、以及不同 teacher/student 组合的完整表格。精读时应去 §3–§6 的图表中补齐这些信息。
summary.reading_guide:
精读建议（must_read，建议 2–3 小时，带着复现实验的目的读）：
1) §3 Phenomenology：重点找“两个条件”的量化定义与判据（thinking-pattern consistency 的具体指标、k 的选择、阈值/相关性），以及 reverse distillation 的实验设置（同数据同配方如何定义、为何导致 indistinguishable）。
2) §4 Mechanism：精读 token 级分析图（overlap ratio 曲线、entropy gap、probability mass concentration），以及“只监督 overlap tokens≈全 top-k”的对照实验——这是全文最关键的机制证据，直接影响你如何设计更稳的 OPD loss。
3) §5 Recipe：把 cold start 与 prompt selection 当成可落地配方读，关注：warmup 需要多长、prompt mixing 比例、entropy 下降的副作用如何监控。
4) §6 Cost/Instability：重点看“深度越长 reward 越差”的定量曲线与不稳定传播分析；如果你做 RL-pretrain/agent 轨迹蒸馏，这部分决定 OPD 的适用边界。

值得深挖的研究点：
- 能否把 overlap ratio 作为训练时的在线诊断/早停信号？
- 能否设计显式提升 overlap 的目标（例如对齐 logits 的低秩子空间、或对非重叠 token 做更强的温度/平滑）？
- “teacher 造成局部平坦”这一假设能否用 Hessian/梯度噪声尺度进一步验证，并导出更好的优化器/学习率策略？
- 长轨迹下稠密监督退化：是否需要分段蒸馏、信用分配重加权、或与 outcome reward 混合？

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies why On-Policy Distillation (OPD)—where the student samples its own rollouts and receives dense per-token supervision from a teacher—can be highly effective in some settings yet completely fail in others, sometimes even when the teacher is objectively stronger. It asks: what observable conditions govern OPD success vs failure, what is the token-level mechanism that actually drives learning, and what practical recipes can reliably recover OPD when it breaks.
summary_en.importance:
For foundation-model training research, the contribution is a rare mechanism-driven account of a widely used post-training primitive:
- It replaces the naive "stronger teacher helps" assumption with two testable distributional requirements (thinking-pattern compatibility and genuine novelty beyond the student’s training exposure), which is directly relevant to scaling, continual distillation, and data/recipe design.
- It identifies a concrete locus of effective gradients: the student–teacher top-k overlap tokens, supported by dynamics (overlap growth, entropy-gap closure, probability-mass concentration). This can inform more stable OPD objectives and diagnostics.
- It provides actionable recovery recipes (off-policy cold start; teacher-aligned prompt selection) and analyzes dense-supervision degradation with trajectory depth—highly relevant for long-horizon reasoning and agentic rollouts.

While not a new pretraining objective, it elevates OPD into a measurable, debuggable operator for continual improvement pipelines and potentially RL-pretrain-style self-bootstrapping.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The paper is organized as phenomenology → mechanism → recipe → cost/limits.

1) Phenomenology: two governing conditions.
(A) Thinking-pattern consistency: student and teacher must have compatible next-token distributions, quantified via top-k overlap ratio. If initial overlap is low, OPD often cannot recover even if the teacher scores higher.
(B) Higher benchmark scores do not imply new transferable knowledge: if teacher and student share the same data and training recipe (only scale differs), they may converge to distributions that are indistinguishable from the student’s perspective, leaving little signal for OPD.
Reverse distillation experiments are used to validate these claims and to argue OPD primarily learns "thinking patterns" (distributional behavior) rather than merely chasing benchmark metrics.

2) Token-level mechanism.
Successful OPD shows a consistent signature on student-visited states: increasing top-k overlap, shrinking entropy gap, and the overlap set capturing nearly all probability mass. Failing runs show stagnant overlap and persistent entropy mismatch.
A key test: supervising only the overlap tokens matches full top-k supervision, implying the overlap set is the main carrier of useful gradients.

3) Practical recipes.
- Off-policy cold start: warm up with SFT on teacher-generated rollouts to raise initial overlap, then switch to OPD.
- Teacher-aligned prompt selection: use prompts from the teacher’s post-training distribution to sharpen alignment on high-probability tokens; mitigate entropy collapse by mixing with out-of-distribution prompts.

4) Cost/instability with depth.
Reward quality degrades with trajectory depth; instability starts at later tokens and propagates backward. Even "failing" teachers provide globally informative reward, suggesting failure is due to local optimization geometry (e.g., a locally flat landscape around the student induced by a larger teacher), not purely reward noise.
summary_en.experiments:
From the provided full-text excerpt, the main quantitative/empirical anchors are:
- In successful OPD, top-k overlap ratio increases from 72% to 91%.
- The shared top-k overlap tokens account for 97–99% of the combined probability mass.
- Overlap-only supervision performs on par with full top-k supervision (qualitative claim in the excerpt).
- Failing runs exhibit stagnant overlap and persistent entropy mismatch.
- Reverse distillation indicates same-family 1.5B and 7B teachers can be distributionally indistinguishable to the student, explaining why a stronger teacher may not help.
- Dense supervision degrades with trajectory depth; instability originates at later tokens and propagates backward.

The excerpt does not include full benchmark tables, exact OPD loss details (k, temperature, weighting), training budgets, or prompt/data scales; those should be extracted from Sections 3–6 in the full paper for reproducibility.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Deep-read guide (2–3 hours, aiming to reuse the recipe):
- Section 3 (Phenomenology): focus on how thinking-pattern consistency is measured (top-k overlap definition, choice of k, thresholds) and how "new knowledge" is operationalized in reverse distillation.
- Section 4 (Mechanism): study the plots for overlap ratio, entropy gap, and probability-mass concentration; the overlap-only supervision experiment is the key mechanistic evidence.
- Section 5 (Recipe): treat as an implementation manual—how long the cold start is, how prompts are selected/mixed, and how entropy collapse is monitored.
- Section 6 (Cost/Instability): extract the depth-vs-reward degradation curves and the instability propagation analysis; this sets the boundary for long-horizon reasoning/agentic OPD.

Research angles worth probing: online overlap-based diagnostics/early stopping, objectives that explicitly increase overlap, verifying the "local flatness" hypothesis via curvature/gradient-noise analyses, and hybrid schemes for long trajectories (segmenting, reweighting, mixing outcome rewards).

recommendation.zh: 它改变我对 OPD 的 prior：teacher 更强不等于更好，先检查思维模式一致与 top-k overlap 动力学；建议立刻按其诊断指标复现实验。
recommendation.en: It updates my OPD prior: a stronger teacher isn’t automatically better—check reasoning-mode match and top-k overlap dynamics first; I’d replicate their diagnostics immediately.

paper.title: Lightning OPD: Efficient Post-Training for Large Reasoning Models with Offline On-Policy Distillation

summary.core_problem: 论文要解决的核心问题是：OPD（On-Policy Distillation）在推理/后训练中效果好但强依赖“训练时实时teacher打分（log-prob）”的在线服务，导致基础设施成本高、复现困难；能否把OPD做成离线（预先算好teacher log-prob并复用）同时不掉性能？作者进一步指出：离线OPD失败的根因并不只是“离线近似”，而是一个被忽视但对任何OPD都必要的条件——SFT阶段生成轨迹的teacher与OPD阶段提供分布监督的teacher必须一致（teacher consistency），否则目标函数存在不可消除的偏差，在线/离线都会收敛到次优不动点。
summary.importance:
对后训练范式的贡献很实：
- 方法论层面：把“teacher consistency”提升为OPD管线的必要条件，解释了社区里常见做法（SFT用最强teacher产数据、OPD用另一个teacher做分布监督）为何会系统性伤害OPD，并给出理论化的偏差/不动点解释。这对构建可扩展、可复现的推理模型后训练流水线影响很大。
- 工程与效率层面：提出Lightning OPD把OPD从“必须在线teacher”改造成“离线一次性预计算teacher log-prob”，在保持（甚至超过）标准OPD效果的同时，去掉并行teacher serving，报告约4×训练加速/成本下降。
- 对预训练研究的启发：虽然属于post-training，但它揭示了“数据生成分布与蒸馏监督分布一致性”这一更一般的原则，可迁移到持续学习/自蒸馏/离线RL式预训练（RL pretrain）中：当你用A模型生成轨迹、用B模型提供token级密集监督时，优化目标可能内生偏置，scale数据也不一定能修正。
summary.technical_approach:
1）问题诊断：作者先观察到OPD阶段student相对SFT reference的分布漂移并不大（与近期RLVR分析一致：RL轨迹多为SFT轨迹的重加权子集、KL约束导致靠近reference），因此提出“离线预计算teacher log-prob并复用”看似可行；但朴素离线OPD效果不稳定。
2）关键条件：teacher consistency。OPD涉及两类teacher：
- SFT teacher：用于生成SFT训练轨迹/示范；
- OPD teacher：用于对student rollout给出token级分布（log-prob）与advantage信号。
作者指出两者不一致会在OPD目标中引入不可消除的偏差，使训练无论在线/离线、无论训练多久/数据多大，都收敛到次优固定点；离线情形更糟，因为rollout分布也被“错误teacher生成的SFT轨迹”锁死。
3）Lightning OPD框架（离线OPD的正确打开方式）：
- 选择一个teacher π_T；
- SFT阶段：用该teacher生成的轨迹对base model做SFT，得到reference policy π_ref；
- OPD阶段：从π_ref采样rollouts（固定分布），对这些固定responses一次性预计算同一个teacher π_T 的log-prob并缓存；训练时用缓存的teacher分布做OPD更新，无需在线teacher server。
4）理论结果（论文声称）：在teacher一致时，Lightning OPD与标准OPD共享相同最优解；两者梯度差异在训练过程中有界；离线目标还带来“隐式正则”抑制policy drift，从而不需要显式惩罚项（例如额外KL penalty）。这些结论共同解释了为何“离线可行”以及为何“必须一致”。
summary.experiments:
论文在数学推理与代码任务上评测Lightning OPD：
- 模型对：包含Qwen3-4B学生配Qwen3-8B teacher，以及Qwen3-8B学生配Qwen3-32B teacher等。
- 结论：Lightning OPD在所有基准上匹配或超过标准（在线）OPD；并通过移除并行teacher serving带来约4.0×加速。
- 论文还在引言中给出一个现实管线的反例：SFT数据由QwQ-32B生成，但OPD teacher用Qwen3-32B（不一致），作者预测并验证这种不一致会伤害OPD。
（注：当前提供的全文片段未包含各benchmark的具体分数表、训练token量/步数、OPD损失形式与超参、以及teacher不一致的定量退化幅度；精读时需要重点核对实验章节的数字与消融。）
summary.reading_guide:
精读建议（建议60–90分钟，优先级高）：
- 先精读“teacher consistency”的形式化定义与理论推导：作者如何刻画“不一致导致不可消除偏差/次优固定点”，以及在一致时为何离线与在线共享同一最优解、梯度差异为何有界。
- 重点看实验消融（若正文有）：
  1）一致 vs 不一致teacher的性能差距（最好按任务/模型对分解）；
  2）离线预计算在不同rollout分布（π_ref vs 训练中student）下的敏感性；
  3）“隐式正则防漂移”的证据：例如KL随训练变化、长训练是否更稳。
- 关注工程细节：缓存teacher log-prob的存储/IO开销、token级advantage如何计算、是否需要重算/分片、对长序列与大batch的吞吐影响。
- 值得深挖的研究点：把该一致性原则推广到更一般的“数据生成模型≠监督模型”的蒸馏/持续学习场景；以及是否能在允许不一致时，通过重要性采样/校正项消除偏差（论文声称不可消除，需看其假设边界）。

summary_en.core_problem: OPD (On-Policy Distillation) is effective for post-training reasoning models but typically requires a live teacher server to score every student rollout, creating major infrastructure and reproducibility barriers. The paper asks whether OPD can be made offline by precomputing teacher log-probabilities once and reusing them—then explains why naive offline OPD fails and identifies a necessary condition for any OPD pipeline: the teacher used to generate SFT trajectories must be the same teacher used to provide OPD distributional supervision (teacher consistency).
summary_en.importance:
This is a high-impact post-training paper with clear implications for scalable foundation-model training:
- Conceptual contribution: elevates “teacher consistency” from an implementation detail to a necessary condition, explaining systematic failures when SFT demonstrations come from one model while OPD supervision comes from another. The claim is strong: inconsistency induces an irreducible bias and a suboptimal fixed point even for online OPD, not just offline.
- Practical contribution: Lightning OPD removes the need for parallel teacher serving by caching teacher log-probs offline, reporting ~4× speedup while matching or exceeding standard OPD on reasoning/code benchmarks.
- Broader research lesson relevant to continual learning / self-distillation / RL-pretrain-like pipelines: mixing a data-generation policy and a different token-level supervising policy can bake in objective bias that does not vanish with more compute or data, so “distributional alignment” between generation and supervision matters as much as raw teacher strength.
summary_en.technical_approach:
1) Empirical motivation: student policies in OPD tend to drift only modestly from the SFT reference (consistent with observations that RL trajectories are largely reweighted SFT trajectories and KL constraints keep policies near the reference), suggesting offline reuse of teacher scores might work.
2) Root-cause analysis: OPD implicitly involves two teachers—an SFT teacher that produced the trajectories used to train the reference policy, and an OPD teacher that provides token-level distribution targets/advantages during distillation. If these differ, the OPD objective becomes biased; the paper argues this bias is irreducible and leads to convergence to a suboptimal fixed point regardless of training length or data scale. Offline OPD is further harmed because the rollout distribution is fixed to the (already mismatched) reference.
3) Lightning OPD (offline OPD done right): choose a single teacher π_T; (i) generate SFT trajectories with π_T and fine-tune the base model to obtain π_ref; (ii) sample rollouts from π_ref and precompute π_T log-probabilities once over these fixed responses; (iii) train the student with OPD using cached teacher scores—no live teacher server.
4) Theory claims: under teacher consistency, Lightning OPD shares the same optimum as standard OPD; the gradient discrepancy remains bounded during training; and the offline objective provides implicit regularization that limits policy drift without an explicit penalty term.
summary_en.experiments:
Evaluations are reported on math reasoning and code generation with multiple student–teacher pairs, including Qwen3-4B distilled from Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-8B distilled from Qwen3-32B. The headline results are: Lightning OPD matches or outperforms standard (online) OPD across benchmarks while delivering ~4.0× speedup by eliminating parallel teacher serving. The introduction also highlights a real-world inconsistent setup (SFT trajectories from QwQ-32B but OPD teacher as Qwen3-32B) as a predicted failure mode.
(Note: the provided excerpt does not include detailed score tables, training budgets, or ablation magnitudes; those should be verified in the main experiment section.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
How to read (60–90 minutes, worth a deep pass):
- Start with the formal definition and theoretical section on teacher consistency: locate the exact assumptions under which inconsistency yields an irreducible bias/suboptimal fixed point, and the proof that offline and online share the same optimum when consistent.
- Then read the ablations (if present): consistent vs inconsistent teacher, offline vs online, sensitivity to rollout distribution choice, and evidence for the claimed “implicit regularization” (e.g., KL drift curves).
- Finally, check the engineering details: how teacher log-probs are stored/sharded, I/O overhead, how per-token advantages are computed, and how this scales with long sequences.
- Research follow-ups to consider: whether bias under inconsistency can be corrected via importance weighting or explicit correction terms, and how the principle generalizes to continual/self-distillation pipelines.

recommendation.zh: 必须看其“teacher consistency”结论：SFT 产轨迹与 OPD 打分 teacher 不一致会系统性收敛到次优；动作是把你们蒸馏流水线 teacher 统一并离线缓存 logprob。
recommendation.en: Must-read for the “teacher consistency” constraint: mismatching the SFT trajectory teacher and OPD scoring teacher drives systematic suboptimal convergence; action item—unify teachers and cache logprobs offline.

paper.title: ReasonXL: Shifting LLM Reasoning Language Without Sacrificing Performance

summary.core_problem: 在不损失推理性能的前提下，改变/控制LLM进行推理时使用的“推理语言”（例如从英语迁移到其他语言或特定受控语言）。
summary.importance: 对后训练与可控推理（reasoning control）有启发：涉及推理表征是否语言不变、以及如何在保持能力的同时施加输出/思维语言约束；对多语预训练与对齐也有间接价值。
summary.technical_approach: 从题目推断为一种“ReasonXL”方法：通过指令/数据构造/约束解码或轻量后训练，使模型在生成推理过程时切换到目标语言，同时保持最终答案质量；是否使用蒸馏、对比学习、或双语链式推理对齐未知（无摘要）。
summary.experiments: 无摘要，无法确认评测任务（GSM8K/MATH/BBH等）、目标语言集合、与基线（直接翻译/多语SFT/提示词控制）相比的性能差异与代价。

summary_en.core_problem: Shift/control the language used for LLM reasoning without degrading reasoning performance.
summary_en.importance: Potentially insightful for post-training and controllable reasoning: probes whether reasoning representations are language-invariant and how to enforce a target “reasoning language” while preserving capability; indirectly relevant to multilingual pretraining and alignment.
summary_en.technical_approach: From the title, ReasonXL likely uses instruction/data construction, constrained decoding, or lightweight post-training to force reasoning traces into a target language while maintaining answer quality; whether it relies on distillation, contrastive alignment, or bilingual CoT is unclear (no abstract).
summary_en.experiments: Not available (no abstract): tasks (e.g., GSM8K/MATH/BBH), target languages, baselines, and tradeoffs cannot be verified.

recommendation.zh: 作为“推理表征是否语言无关”的现象备查即可；扫一眼控制强度-性能曲线和失败案例，别花时间抠细节。
recommendation.en: Worth knowing as a datapoint on language-invariant reasoning; just skim the control-strength vs performance curves and failure cases, skip the rest.

paper.title: Continuous Adversarial Flow Models

summary.core_problem: Flow Matching（FM）在视觉生成中常出现“无 guidance 时样本偏离数据分布（out-of-distribution）”的问题。作者认为根因之一是 FM 训练使用固定的欧氏 MSE 速度匹配损失，有限容量模型在这种度量下会产生不符合数据流形的泛化。问题是：能否在连续时间流模型中引入对抗式、可学习的判别准则，以更好地对齐真实数据分布，同时保持连续时间 ODE 生成框架？
summary.importance: 连续时间流模型（CNF/FM 系）是扩散/流生成的重要分支。若能在不依赖 guidance 的情况下显著提升分布匹配与感知质量，将直接改善“无引导采样”的可用性，并为后训练（post-training）现有 FM 模型提供低成本增益路径；同时把 GAN 式判别器优势引入连续时间生成，为统一/融合两类范式提供新接口。
summary.technical_approach:
（must_read 级别：详细技术分析）
1) 观点与动机：FM 通过最小化预测速度场与目标条件速度的 L2/MSE 来学习概率流的边际速度场。理论上无限容量可收敛到真流，但有限容量下，固定欧氏损失并不“流形感知”，导致错误泛化与 OOD 样本；而固定感知网络作为度量又可能被生成器“hacking”。
2) 核心方法：提出 Continuous Adversarial Flow Models（CAFM），把对抗训练引入连续时间流建模。与离散时间的 Adversarial Flow Models（AFM）不同，CAFM 在连续时间（ODE）框架下，用“学习到的判别器”替代固定的 MSE 准则来指导速度场学习，从而在有限容量情形诱导出不同的广义分布（generalized distribution），经验上更贴近目标数据分布。
3) 训练范式：主要定位为对现有 FM 的 post-training（微调/后训练），以较小训练成本改善分布对齐；也可从头训练。方法强调：FM 与 CAFM 目标真流相同，差异主要来自训练目标导致的泛化行为不同。
4) 预期效果机制：判别器相较点对点 L2 更敏感于纹理、锐度、轮廓等感知细节，可能更好刻画数据流形；联合训练判别器可缓解固定特征度量被利用的问题。
summary.experiments: ImageNet 256×256 类条件生成：对 latent-space SiT 的 guidance-free FID 从 8.26 提升到 3.63；对 pixel-space JiT 从 7.17 提升到 3.57，且仅需约 10 epochs 后训练。Guided 生成也有提升：SiT FID 2.06→1.53，JiT 1.86→1.80。文本到图像实验：GenEval 0.81→0.85，DPG 83.7→85.2。整体结论是：对抗式连续流后训练能显著改善无引导分布匹配与感知质量，并兼顾有引导场景。
summary.reading_guide:
（must_read：精读建议）
- 精读 Introduction：抓住作者对 FM “OOD 与欧氏度量”根因的论证链条，以及与 Riemannian FM、感知损失、GAN/AFM 的关系定位。
- 精读 Background（FM 推导部分）：确保理解条件速度/边际速度、FM 目标为何依赖度量性质（文中提到的准则条件），这是 CAFM 替换损失的理论接口。
- 精读 CAFM 方法章节：重点看对抗目标如何在连续时间/ODE 设定中定义（判别器输入是什么、与时间 t 的耦合方式、训练稳定性技巧、与 AFM 的关键差异）。
- 精读实验：重点看“post-training 设置”（训练轮数、学习率、判别器结构/正则、是否改变采样器）、以及 guidance-free 与 guided 的对比，判断收益来自分布对齐还是仅锐化。
（skim：泛读建议）
- 只想快速获取结论：读 Introduction + ImageNet 主表（SiT/JiT 的 FID 改善）+ 文本到图像指标（GenEval/DPG）。
summary.authors_note: 作者主张 FM 的固定 MSE 速度匹配在有限容量下会产生不符合数据流形的泛化，从而导致无 guidance 的 OOD 样本；通过在连续时间流模型中引入可学习判别器的对抗目标（CAFM），可作为对现有 FM 的高性价比后训练手段，显著提升分布匹配与感知质量。

summary_en.core_problem: Flow Matching (FM) often produces out-of-distribution samples in visual generation unless guidance is applied. The paper argues a key reason is the fixed Euclidean MSE objective for velocity matching: with finite model capacity, this non-manifold-aware metric induces undesirable generalization. The question is how to incorporate adversarial, learned criteria into continuous-time flow models (ODE/CNF setting) to better match the true data distribution while retaining continuous-time generation.
summary_en.importance: Continuous-time flow models are a major alternative to diffusion-style generators. Improving guidance-free fidelity and distribution matching would make unguided sampling more practical and provides a cost-effective post-training route for existing FM models. Conceptually, it also bridges GAN-style discriminators with continuous-time flow modeling, offering a new integration point between two paradigms.
summary_en.technical_approach:
(must_read level: detailed technical analysis)
1) Motivation: FM learns the marginal velocity field of a probability flow by minimizing an L2/MSE loss between predicted and target conditional velocities. While infinite-capacity models can recover the true flow, finite-capacity models trained under a fixed Euclidean metric may generalize off the data manifold, yielding OOD samples. Using a fixed perceptual network as the metric can be exploited (“generator hacking”), motivating joint training of the criterion.
2) Method: Continuous Adversarial Flow Models (CAFMs) introduce adversarial training into continuous-time flow modeling. Unlike discrete-time Adversarial Flow Models (AFMs), CAFMs operate in continuous time (ODE/CNF) and replace the fixed MSE criterion with a learned discriminator to guide learning. This changes the effective generalized distribution induced under finite capacity and empirically yields samples closer to the target distribution.
3) Training usage: Primarily proposed as post-training (finetuning) of existing FM models for efficiency, though it can also train from scratch. The paper emphasizes FM and CAFM target the same ground-truth flow; differences arise mainly from finite-capacity generalization under different objectives.
4) Intuition: Discriminators are more sensitive to perceptual details (texture, sharpness, contours) than pointwise L2 losses and may better capture manifold structure; jointly learned criteria mitigate fixed-metric exploitation.
summary_en.experiments: On class-conditional ImageNet 256px: post-training improves guidance-free FID for latent-space SiT from 8.26 to 3.63 and for pixel-space JiT from 7.17 to 3.57 with ~10 epochs of finetuning. Guided generation also improves (SiT 2.06→1.53, JiT 1.86→1.80). In text-to-image, GenEval increases 0.81→0.85 and DPG 83.7→85.2. Overall, adversarial continuous-time post-training substantially improves unguided fidelity/distribution matching and also benefits guided settings.
summary_en.reading_guide:
(must_read: deep reading)
- Read Introduction to understand the claimed root cause (Euclidean metric → manifold-mismatched generalization) and positioning vs Riemannian FM, perceptual losses, GANs, and AFMs.
- Read Background carefully (FM derivations): conditional vs marginal velocity and why the FM objective depends on properties of the distance/criterion—this is the theoretical hook for swapping MSE with a learned discriminator.
- Read the CAFM method section in detail: how the adversarial objective is defined in continuous time/ODE, what the discriminator sees, how time t is incorporated, stability/regularization tricks, and the key differences from discrete-time AFM.
- Read experiments focusing on the post-training protocol (epochs, optimizer, discriminator architecture/regularization, sampler changes) and compare guidance-free vs guided to judge whether gains are true distribution alignment vs mere sharpening.
(skim: quick reading)
- For takeaways only: read Introduction + the main ImageNet FID table (SiT/JiT) + the text-to-image GenEval/DPG results.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors argue that FM’s fixed MSE velocity-matching objective leads to manifold-mismatched generalization under finite capacity, causing OOD unguided samples. By introducing a learned discriminator into continuous-time flow training (CAFM), they provide an efficient post-training recipe that markedly improves guidance-free fidelity and distribution matching, with additional gains under guidance.

recommendation.zh: 只需看对抗判别损失如何插进连续时间FM训练与稳定性ablation；若成立，后训练给现有FM加个判别器可能是低成本增益。
recommendation.en: Skim the exact adversarial objective insertion into continuous-time FM and the stability ablations; if it holds, adding a discriminator as post-training for existing FM could be a cheap win.

paper.title: Efficient RL Training for LLMs with Experience Replay
paper.abstract: While Experience Replay - the practice of storing rollouts and reusing them multiple times during training - is a foundational technique in general RL, it remains largely unexplored in LLM post-training due to the prevailing belief that fresh, on-policy data is essential for high performance. In this work, we challenge this assumption.
